title: What Happens to Your Old Phone Number, and What to Do First
html:
A phone number you stop using does not disappear. Mobile operators can give it to a new customer after some time. If your bank, UPI app, email or social accounts still use that number, the next owner may receive your messages or codes. So move your accounts off the number first, then let it go.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026.

Sources last checked: 10 Oct 2026.

How long before it can be reused?

TRAI's FAQ says disconnected mobile numbers may be reallocated to new subscribers, by the telecom service providers, after expiry of 90 days.

As reported by LiveLaw (3 November 2023), TRAI told the Supreme Court in Rajeswari v. Union of India, WP(C) 699/2021, that a deactivated number is not given to a new subscriber for at least 90 days. The Court said the earlier subscriber should delete the WhatsApp account linked to the old number and erase its data from devices and cloud. WhatsApp said it removes old data of an account that was inactive for 45 days and is then activated on another device.

Ask your operator when your old number could be reallocated.

Move these off the old number first

  1. Bank and UPI. Change the registered mobile number with your bank, and then check the UPI apps you use. Ask your bank how to do it safely, in a branch, in its official app or by its official number.
  2. Google. In your Google Account open Security and sign-in, then Recovery phone, and change it. Google says changes to recovery details can take up to 7 days to take effect, so do it early. If the old number is also a second step, move that to an authenticator app or a passkey: which method to use.
  3. WhatsApp. Google's page on moving WhatsApp says you cannot transfer WhatsApp data to a new phone number, and that you can change your number on the old phone first. See moving WhatsApp to a new phone.
  4. Other accounts that send you codes: email, social media, shopping, food delivery, e-commerce, government and tax portals.
  5. People: tell family and close contacts your new number.

If you already gave the number up

Use the other route to each account (email recovery, backup codes) and change the number from inside the account. If you think a stranger now has your old number, change the passwords for accounts tied to it and turn on a stronger second step. Our account recovery guide shows the order.

Check the numbers in your name

Sanchar Saathi's "Know your mobile connections" service lets you log in with an OTP and see the mobile connections registered in your name, and report ones that are not yours or that you no longer need. Check it once a year.

What to do next

  1. List every account that uses the old number.
  2. Change the number in each, starting with banking and email.
  3. Only then stop using the number, and check your connections on Sanchar Saathi.
